    {
      "category": "readme",
      "severity": "橙",
      "path": "README.md",
      "name": "Notable Updates",
      "message": "官方更新小节变化",
      "before": "## Latest update — August 13th, 2026\n\nThis release:\n\n- Adds key configuration parameters (including weights used to blend predicted action values into a score for a post)\n- Adds code for systems that impact whether a post is filtered from the For You feed\n- Replaces the Phoenix demonstration model with the code used to train the models the feed uses, as well as synthetic data generation code so one can run a proof-of-concept training run of Phoenix.\n\nAmong new systems included are:\n\n1. **Visibility filtering:** [`visibility-filtering/`](visibility-filtering/) determines whether to show a post, drop it, or show it behind an interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",
      "after": "## Latest Updates\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior. We've [added comments](home-mixer/params/param.rs) [to the code](home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs) so that LLMs or people reading it are more likely to understand it correctly.\n- **Brazil 2026 Elections.** As [announced by X](https://x.com/XBR/status/2088341967864320507?s=20), in accordance with Brazilian electoral law, For You now runs `Brazil2026ElectionFilter`, which removes posts from accounts reported to Brazil's Electoral Court for the 2026 election, unless the viewer explicitly follows the account. A benefit of open-source is that you can see that changes like this exist, and exactly how they work — take a [look at the code](home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs).\n\n### August 13th, 2026\n\nThis release:\n\n- Adds key configuration parameters (including weights used to blend predicted action values into a score for a post)\n- Adds code for systems that impact whether a post is filtered from the For You feed\n- Replaces the Phoenix demonstration model with the code used to train the models the feed uses, as well as synthetic data generation code so one can run a proof-of-concept training run of Phoenix.\n\nAmong new systems included are:\n\n1. **Visibility filtering:** [`visibility-filtering/`](visibility-filtering/) determines whether to show a post, drop it, or show it behind an interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",
      "line_before": null,
      "line_after": null,
      "evidence": "## Latest Updates\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior. We've [added comments](home-mixer/params/param.rs) [to the code](home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs) so that LLMs or people reading it are more likely to understand it correctly.\n- **Brazil 2026 Elections.** As [announced by X](https://x.com/XBR/status/2088341967864320507?s=20), in accordance with Brazilian electoral law, For You now runs `Brazil2026ElectionFilter`, which removes posts from accounts reported to Brazil's Electoral Court for the 2026 election, unless the viewer explicitly follows the account. A benefit of open-source is that you can see that changes like this exist, and exactly how they work — take a [look at the code](home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs).\n\n### August 13th, 2026\n\nThis release:\n\n- Adds key configuration parameters (including weights used to blend predicted action values into a score for a post)\n- Adds code for systems that impact whether a post is filtered from the For You feed\n- Replaces the Phoenix demonstration model with the code used to train the models the feed uses, as well as synthetic data generation code so one can run a proof-of-concept training run of Phoenix.\n\nAmong new systems included are:\n\n1. **Visibility filtering:** [`visibility-filtering/`](visibility-filtering/) determines whether to show a post, drop it, or show it behind an interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",

      "name": "Notable Updates",
      "message": "官方更新小节变化",
      "before": "## Latest Updates\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior. We've [added comments](home-mixer/params/param.rs) [to the code](home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs) so that LLMs or people reading it are more likely to understand it correctly.\n- **Brazil 2026 Elections.** As [announced by X](https://x.com/XBR/status/2088341967864320507?s=20), in accordance with Brazilian electoral law, For You now runs `Brazil2026ElectionFilter`, which removes posts from accounts reported to Brazil's Electoral Court for the 2026 election, unless the viewer explicitly follows the account. A benefit of open-source is that you can see that changes like this exist, and exactly how they work — take a [look at the code](home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs).\n\n### August 13th, 2026\n\nThis release:\n\n- Adds key configuration parameters (including weights used to blend predicted action values into a score for a post)\n- Adds code for systems that impact whether a post is filtered from the For You feed\n- Replaces the Phoenix demonstration model with the code used to train the models the feed uses, as well as synthetic data generation code so one can run a proof-of-concept training run of Phoenix.\n\nAmong new systems included are:\n\n1. **Visibility filtering:** [`visibility-filtering/`](visibility-filtering/) determines whether to show a post, drop it, or show it behind an interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",

interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",

      "before": "## Notable Updates\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior. We've [added comments](home-mixer/params/param.rs) [to the code](home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs) so that LLMs or people reading it are more likely to understand it correctly.\n- **Brazil 2026 Elections.** As [announced by X](https://x.com/XBR/status/2088341967864320507?s=20), in accordance with Brazilian electoral law, For You now runs `Brazil2026ElectionFilter`, which removes posts from accounts reported to Brazil's Electoral Court for the 2026 election, unless the viewer explicitly follows the account. *(Account list updated August 25, 2026.)* A benefit of open-source is that you can see that changes like this exist, and exactly how they work — take a [look at the code](home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs).\n\n### August 13th, 2026\n\nThis release:\n\n- Adds key configuration parameters (including weights used to blend predicted action values into a score for a post)\n- Adds code for systems that impact whether a post is filtered from the For You feed\n- Replaces the Phoenix demonstration model with the code used to train the models the feed uses, as well as synthetic data generation code so one can run a proof-of-concept training run of Phoenix.\n\nAmong new systems included are:\n\n1. **Visibility filtering:** [`visibility-filtering/`](visibility-filtering/) determines whether to show a post, drop it, or show it behind an interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",

      "category": "readme",
      "severity": "橙",
      "path": "README.md",
      "name": "Notable Updates",
      "message": "官方更新小节变化",
      "before": "## Notable Updates\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior. We've [added comments](home-mixer/params/param.rs) [to the code](home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs) so that LLMs or people reading it are more likely to understand it correctly.\n- **Brazil 2026 Elections.** As [announced by X](https://x.com/XBR/status/2088341967864320507?s=20), in accordance with Brazilian electoral law, For You now runs `Brazil2026ElectionFilter`, which removes posts from accounts reported to Brazil's Electoral Court for the 2026 election, unless the viewer explicitly follows the account. *(Account list updated August 27, 2026.)* A benefit of open-source is that you can see that changes like this exist, and exactly how they work — take a [look at the code](home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs).\n\n### August 13th, 2026\n\nThis release:\n\n- Adds key configuration parameters (including weights used to blend predicted action values into a score for a post)\n- Adds code for systems that impact whether a post is filtered from the For You feed\n- Replaces the Phoenix demonstration model with the code used to train the models the feed uses, as well as synthetic data generation code so one can run a proof-of-concept training run of Phoenix.\n\nAmong new systems included are:\n\n1. **Visibility filtering:** [`visibility-filtering/`](visibility-filtering/) determines whether to show a post, drop it, or show it behind an interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",

      "name": "Notable Updates",
      "message": "官方更新小节变化",
      "before": "## Notable Updates\n\n### September 18th, 2026\n\n- **[Under the Hood](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool).** Reports now include information about whether one's account or posts have had their visibility limited because of required compliance with law(s). For example, you'll be able to see if any of your posts were withheld from showing in a country following a legal demand — and which country.\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior. We've [added comments](home-mixer/params/param.rs) [to the code](home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs) so that LLMs or people reading it are more likely to understand it correctly.\n- **Brazil 2026 Elections.** As [announced by X](https://x.com/XBR/status/2088341967864320507?s=20), in accordance with Brazilian electoral law, For You now runs `Brazil2026ElectionFilter`, which removes posts from accounts reported to Brazil's Electoral Court for the 2026 election, unless the viewer explicitly follows the account. *(Account list updated August 27, 2026.)* A benefit of open-source is that you can see that changes like this exist, and exactly how they work — take a [look at the code](home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs).\n\n### August 13th, 2026\n\nThis release:\n\n- Adds key configuration parameters (including weights used to blend predicted action values into a score for a post)\n- Adds code for systems that impact whether a post is filtered from the For You feed\n- Replaces the Phoenix demonstration model with the code used to train the models the feed uses, as well as synthetic data generation code so one can run a proof-of-concept training run of Phoenix.\n\nAmong new systems included are:\n\n1. **Visibility filtering:** [`visibility-filtering/`](visibility-filtering/) determines whether to show a post, drop it, or show it behind an interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",
      "after": "## Notable Updates\n\n### September 18th, 2026\n\n- **[Under the Hood](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool).** Reports now include information about whether one's account or posts have had their visibility limited because of required compliance with law(s). For example, you'll be able to see if any of your posts were withheld from showing in a country following a legal demand — and which country.\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior. We've [added comments](home-mixer/params/param.rs) [to the code](xai-value-model/scoring.rs) so that LLMs or people reading it are more likely to understand it correctly.\n- **Brazil 2026 Elections.** name: String,\n+    pub(super) level: SafetyLevel,\n+    pub(super) viewer: ViewerFeatures,\n+    pub(super) candidate: HydratedTweetCandidate,\n+    expected: Verdict,\n+}\n+\n+impl Row {\n+    fn expand(self) -> impl Iterator<Item = CorpusCase> {\n+        let Row { name, post, expect } = self;\n+        expect.into_iter().map(move |(level, role, expected)| {\n+            let mut candidate = post.clone();\n+            let (role_name, viewer) = match role {\n+                Role::NonFollower => (\"non_follower\", viewer(VIEWER_ID)),\n+                Role::Author => (\"author\", viewer(candidate.author_id)),\n+                Role::Follower => {\n+                    candidate.relationship.viewer_follows_author = true;\n+                    (\"follower\", viewer(VIEWER_ID))\n+                }\n+                Role::LoggedOut => {\n+                    candidate.relationship = ViewerAuthorRelationship::default();\n+                    candidate.blocked_by = ViewerBlockedBy::default();\n+                    (\"logged_out\", logged_out_viewer())\n+                }\n+                Role::As(role_name, viewer) => (role_name, viewer),\n+            };\n+            CorpusCase {\n+                name: format!(\"{name}/{level:?}/{role_name}\"),\n+                level,\n+                viewer,\n+                candidate,\n+                expected,\n+            }\n+        })\n+    }\n+}\n+\n+fn deciders(verdict: &Verdict) -> Vec<&'static str> {\n+    match verdict {\n+        Verdict::Withheld(decided) => vec![decided.by],\n+        Verdict::Shown { media, engagement } => media\n+            .iter()\n+            .map(|blur| blur.by)\n+            .chain(engagement.iter().map(|limit| limit.by))\n+            .collect(),\n+    }\n+}\n+\n+#[test]\n+fn golden_corpus_pins_policy_verdicts() {\n+    let rule_engine = RuleEngine::for_tests();\n+    let cases = corpus();\n+    let names: BTreeSet<&str> = cases.iter().map(|c| c.name.as_str()).collect();\n+    assert_eq!(names.len(), cases.len(), \"duplicate corpus case name\");\n+    let mut failures = Vec::new();\n+    for case in cases {\n+        let verdict = rule_engine.evaluate(case.level, &case.viewer, &case.candidate);\n+        if matches!(&case.expected, Verdict::Shown { media: Some(_), .. }) {\n+            let (action, reason) = proto_action(verdict.clone());\n+            assert_eq!(action.encode_to_vec(), [0x20, 0x01], \"{}\", case.name);\n+            assert_eq!(\n+                reason.unwrap().encode_to_vec(),\n+                [0x08, 0x01],\n+                \"{}\",\n+                case.name\n+            );\n+        }\n+        if verdict != case.expected {\n+            failures.push(format!(\n+                \"{} [{:?}]:\\n  expected {:?}\\n  got      {:?}\",\n+                case.name, case.level, case.expected, verdict,\n+            ));\n+        }\n+    }\n+    assert!(\n+        failures.is_empty(),\n+        \"{} corpus case(s) diverged:\\n{}\",\n+        failures.len(),\n+        failures.join(\"\\n\")\n+    );\n+}\n+\n+#[test]\n+fn every_wired_rule_decides_a_corpus_case() TimelineHomeHydration,\n+        ImmersiveExpandedRecommendations,\n+    ]\n+    .into_iter()\n+    .flat_map(|level| rule_engine.wired_rule_names(level))\n+    .collect();\n+    let deciders: BTreeSet<&'static str> = corpus()\n+        .iter()\n+        .flat_map(|c| deciders(&c.expected))\n+        .collect();\n+    let missing: Vec<&&'static str> = wired.difference(&deciders).collect();\n+    assert!(\n+        missing.is_empty(),\n+        \"rules wired in RuleEngine but never the decider of any corpus case: {missing:?}\"\n+    );\n+}\n+\n+pub(super) fn corpus() -> Vec<CorpusCase> {\n+    rows().into_iter().flat_map(Row::expand).collect()\n+}\n+\n+fn rows() -> Vec<Row> {\n+    [\n+        baseline::rows(),\n+        relationship::rows(),\n+        author_state::rows(),\n+        tweet_label::rows(),\n+        tweet_state::rows(),\n+        takedown::rows(),\n+        age_gating::rows(),\n+        exclusive_content::rows(),\n+        conversation_control::rows(),\n+        interstitial::rows(),\n+        oon_media::rows(),\n+        oon_tweet_label::rows(),\n+        oon_user_label::rows(),\n+       "before": "## Notable Updates\n\n### September 18th, 2026\n\n- **[Under the Hood](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool).** Reports now include information about whether one's account or posts have had their visibility limited because of required compliance with law(s). For example, you'll be able to see if any of your posts were withheld from showing in a country following a legal demand — and which country.\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior. We've [added comments](home-mixer/params/param.rs) [to the code](xai-value-model/scoring.rs) so that LLMs or people reading it are more likely to understand it correctly.\n- **Brazil 2026 Elections.** As [announced by X](https://x.com/XBR/status/2088341967864320507?s=20), in accordance with Brazilian electoral law, For You now runs `Brazil2026ElectionFilter`, which removes posts from accounts reported to Brazil's Electoral Court for the 2026 election, unless the viewer explicitly follows the account. *(Account list updated August 27, 2026.)* A benefit of open-source is that you can see that changes like this exist, and exactly how they work — take a [look at the code](home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs).\n\n### August 13th, 2026\n\nThis release:\n\n- Adds key configuration parameters (including weights used to blend predicted action values into a score for a post)\n- Adds code for systems that impact whether a post is filtered from the For You feed\n- Replaces the Phoenix demonstration model with the code used to train the models the feed uses, as well as synthetic data generation code so one can run a proof-of-concept training run of Phoenix.\n\nAmong new systems included are:\n\n1. **Visibility filtering:** [`visibility-filtering/`](visibility-filtering/) determines whether to show a post, drop it, or show it behind an interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",
      "after": "## Notable Updates\n\n### September 18th, 2026\n\n- **[Under the Hood](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool).** Reports now include information about whether one's account or posts have had their visibility limited because of required compliance with law(s). For example, you'll be able to see if any of your posts were withheld from showing in a country following a legal demand — and which country.\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior. We've [added comments](home-mixer/params/param.rs) [to the code](xai-value-model/scoring.rs) so that LLMs or people reading it are more likely to understand it correctly.\n- **Brazil 2026 Elections.** As [announced by X](https://x.com/XBR/status/2088341967864320507?s=20), in accordance with Brazilian electoral law, For You now runs `Brazil2026ElectionFilter`, which removes posts from accounts reported to Brazil's Electoral Court for the 2026 election, unless the viewer explicitly follows the account. *(Account list updated September 29, 2026.)* A benefit of open-source is that you can see that changes like this exist, and exactly how they work — take a [look at the code](home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs).\n\n### August 13th, 2026\n\nThis release:\n\n- Adds key configuration parameters (including weights used to blend predicted action values into a score for a post)\n- Adds code for systems that impact whether a post is filtered from the For You feed\n- Replaces the Phoenix demonstration model with the code used to train the models the feed uses, as well as synthetic data generation code so one can run a proof-of-concept training run of Phoenix.\n\nAmong new systems included are:\n\n1. **Visibility filtering:** [`visibility-filtering/`](visibility-filtering/) determines whether to show a post, drop it, or show it behind an interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",

      "before": "## Notable Updates\n\n### September 18th, 2026\n\n- **[Under the Hood](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool).** Reports now include information about whether one's account or posts have had their visibility limited because of required compliance with law(s). For example, you'll be able to see if any of your posts were withheld from showing in a country following a legal demand — and which country.\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior. We've [added comments](home-mixer/params/param.rs) [to the code](xai-value-model/scoring.rs) so that LLMs or people reading it are more likely to understand it correctly.\n- **Brazil 2026 Elections.** As [announced by X](https://x.com/XBR/status/2088341967864320507?s=20), in accordance with Brazilian electoral law, For You now runs `Brazil2026ElectionFilter`, which removes posts from accounts reported to Brazil's Electoral Court for the 2026 election, unless the viewer explicitly follows the account. *(Account list updated September 29, 2026.)* A benefit of open-source is that you can see that changes like this exist, and exactly how they work — take a [look at the code](home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs).\n\n### August 13th, 2026\n\nThis release:\n\n- Adds key configuration parameters (including weights used to blend predicted action values into a score for a post)\n- Adds code for systems that impact whether a post is filtered from the For You feed\n- Replaces the Phoenix demonstration model with the code used to train the models the feed uses, as well as synthetic data generation code so one can run a proof-of-concept training run of Phoenix.\n\nAmong new systems included are:\n\n1. **Visibility filtering:** [`visibility-filtering/`](visibility-filtering/) determines whether to show a post, drop it, or show it behind an interstitial.\n2. **The systems that produce labels that drive visibility filtering's responses:** rules that apply labels ([`botmaker/`](botmaker/), [`botmaker-rules/`](botmaker-rules/), [`scarecrow/`](scarecrow/)), models that score accounts on various dimensions ([`agatha/`](agatha/), [`bdsm/`](bdsm/), [`user-cred-v2/`](user-cred-v2/)), models that examine images and video ([`media-model-proxy/`](media-model-proxy/), [`clip/`](clip/)), and enforcement ([`abuse-enforcement-service/`](abuse-enforcement-service/)).\n3. **Phoenix model code:** [`phoenix/`](phoenix/) now contains code that trains and runs the model, plus synthetic data generation.\n4. **SimClusters:** [`simclusters/`](simclusters/), an additional source of posts from accounts the viewer does not follow that is called in retrieval alongside Thunder and Phoenix retrieval.\n\nThis update is also paired with a new [**Under the Hood**](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool) transparency tool that allows people to see aggregate statistics about the labels on their account and posts that can limit visibility.\n\n---",
      "after": "## Notable Updates\n\n### September 18th, 2026\n\n- **[Under the Hood](#under-the-hood-label-transparency-tool).** Reports now include information about whether one's account or posts have had their visibility limited because of required compliance with law(s). For example, you'll be able to see if any of your posts were withheld from showing in a country following a legal demand — and which country.\n\n### August 14th, 2026\n\nNotable updates:\n\n- **How weights work.** There's a common misconception about how weights related to actions (e.g. Like, Share, Block, Report, etc) work in ranking. The weights scale the predicted probabilities of such actions (or predicted continuous values, e.g. dwell time) — they do *not* scale the raw engagement counts, so e.g. it'd be incorrect to see that a report has 468 times higher weight than a like and conclude that e.g. \"1 report cancels out 468 likes\". The weights are a multiple on your own predicted probability of Liking, Reporting, etc, which is substantially driven by your own behavior.
